classifiedFindings.label: L-14
classifiedFindings.title: totalWithdrawal Phase-2 executes the LIVE client balance, not the Phase-1 announced snapshot; story-048 retiming (6h/72h, 78h total) shrinks the community reaction window 4x while three documentation sources still claim 24h/48h
classifiedFindings.plausibility: n/a (not a High; no external attack scenario exists — executor is onlyOwner, proceeds go to owner())
classifiedFindings.fileLine: src/AYieldStrategy.sol:822-837 (Phase-1 snapshot into state.balance), :846-860 (Phase-2 passes cached amount), :84-86 (WAITING_PERIOD=6h, EXECUTION_WINDOW=72h, 78h total — source-verified), :414 (stale '24-hour waiting / 48-hour window' docstring — source-verified); src/concreteYieldStrategies/ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:209-240 (_totalWithdraw ignores the amount parameter and re-reads clientBalances live — source-verified); src/interfaces/IYieldStrategy.sol:101 (stale)

classification.assetImpact: No external asset theft, loss, or compromise. The two-phase totalWithdrawal is an owner-only emergency-migration path whose proceeds are transferred to owner() for redistribution; deposits arriving between Phase 1 and Phase 2 are swept in excess of the announced figure, but the destination is the trusted owner and value-conservation holds. The harmed asset is INFORMATIONAL: the anti-rug commitment that the announced amount and documented reaction window represent to the community. WithdrawalExecuted additionally emits the cached (announced) amount rather than the actual swept amount (open L-06-run11), so on-chain observers cannot even detect the drift from events.
attackPath: 1. (Owner-initiated, legitimate-migration context) Owner calls totalWithdrawal Phase 1; _initiateWithdrawal snapshots state.balance = live balance and emits WithdrawalInitiated with that announced amount.
2. During the (now 6h, was 24h) waiting period plus the (now 72h) execution window, authorized clients continue depositing; clientBalances[token][client] grows past the announcement.

3. Owner calls Phase 2; _executeWithdrawal passes the cached snapshot down, but ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy._totalWithdraw IGNORES the amount parameter — it re-reads clientBalances live and sells proportional shares for the FULL live balance (Tier-3 detector: executed 1,209,632e18 vs announced 278,585e18 after a mid-window deposit at the 6h boundary).

4. The full live balance lands at owner(); WithdrawalExecuted emits the stale announced figure. Community watchers sized to the documented 24h window and the announced amount observe neither the true timing nor the true amount.

5. No step is exploitable by an external party; every trigger is onlyOwner and the recipient is the owner. The hazard is that a competent, NON-malicious owner running a legitimate migration unknowingly sweeps client deposits made after the announcement, and the protocol's documented transparency commitment (3 doc sources still say 24h/48h) materially overstates the community's actual reaction window (6h).
classification.likelihood: low-moderate as an operational event (any migration with active depositors and a mid-window deposit triggers the drift mechanically), but ZERO as an external exploit — no permissionless trigger exists.
classification.assumptions: Owner is non-malicious (Law 3). Clients are protocol-owned, owner-curated contracts. The drift direction that matters here is live > announced (the shrank/zero direction is the separately-tracked benign L-13).
classification.externalRequirements: None benefit an external party. Mid-window client deposits are the only precondition for the drift; story-048's retiming is unconditional.

classifiedFindings.lawBasis: Law-3 non-obvious owner/operator footgun + commitment-transparency weakening. Surprise test PASSES: an owner reading 'Phase 2: Executes withdrawal' against the Phase-1 announcement event would be surprised that execution sweeps the live (larger) balance, and anyone reading the three 24h/48h doc sources would size community-reaction SLAs 4x too generously. Law-1 check (FAITH-15-005): the 6h retiming is story-blessed and NOT an unsafe story, because zero-delay owner exfiltration already exists via emergencyWithdraw (no timelock, works while paused — standing C-01); the waiting period was never the binding rug protection. That domination argument is precisely why this cannot exceed Low.
classifiedFindings.documentationCheck: NOT-BLESSED. knownIssuesCount=0. designDecision #5 documents the two-phase mechanism at the OLD 24h/48h timings — it blesses the window's existence, not live-over-snapshot execution semantics, and is itself stale (doc leg carried by F-05/FAITH-15-004). No systemAssumption covers inter-phase deposit sweep or the retiming.
classifiedFindings.h02Boundary: NOT a re-escalation of H-02 (7b19ceec, status false-positive — ledger-authoritative; the invariant-results.json 'downgraded-to-centralization' string is wrong per DISC-15-001). H-02's adjudicated-and-rejected claims were the High theft framing (circular/owner-funded) and the underflow brick (spurious symbolic artifact); both stay suppressed. This entry's root-cause class — announced-vs-executed commitment-transparency gap as an operational hazard PLUS the diff-new story-048 retiming — was never adjudicated, carries a deliberately distinct fingerprint, and is capped at Low.

severityRationale.notHigh: No assets can be stolen, lost, or compromised by any external party: every trigger is onlyOwner, proceeds go to owner(), value-conservation holds. There is no attack path at all, let alone one without hypotheticals.
severityRationale.notMedium: C4 Medium requires protocol function/availability impact or a value leak with stated assumptions. Neither holds: the migration path functions (it over-performs, not under-performs); no value leaks outside the protocol/owner boundary; user availability is unaffected. Framing the transparency weakening as Medium would also implicitly re-litigate the rejected H-02/rug surface against the Law-1 finding that emergencyWithdraw (0h) already dominates — i.e. the marginal protection lost is on a path that was never binding.
severityRationale.landsLow: Operational hazard / state-handling per C4 QA-Low: announced-vs-executed drift on an owner emergency path, compounded by a misleading event (L-06-run11) and 4x-stale reaction-window documentation. Non-obvious consequence, real monitoring impact, safe-config guidance available — exactly the Law-3 footgun profile, reported at Low.

classifiedFindings.tier3Evidence: Detector invariant invariant_P3_PATTERN001_announcedAmountFaithful fails by design under forge and Medusa (executed 1209632.69e18 > announced 278585.41e18 after mid-window deposit at the 6h boundary). Window-boundary tests confirm the 6h/72h/78h constants are implemented correctly.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Pin Phase-2 execution to min(announced snapshot, live balance) or require re-initiation when the live balance exceeds the announced figure; fix WithdrawalExecuted to emit the actual swept amount (with L-06-run11); update the 24h/48h documentation at AYieldStrategy.sol:414, IYieldStrategy.sol:101, and registry designDecision #5 (F-05); refresh C-01 report text and off-chain monitoring SLAs to the 6h reaction window.
classifiedFindings.justification: Owner-only commitment-transparency drift plus story-blessed retiming with stale disclosure; no external attack path, no value leak, conservation verified — held at Low (Law-3 operational hazard), deliberately NOT a revival of the false-positive H-02 High framing.
classifiedFindings.noOverstatement: Confirmed. Candidate Low confirmed at Low; not upgraded; H-02 suppression boundary and FAITH-15-005 Law-1 cap both honored.

classifiedFindings.label: L-15
classifiedFindings.title: story-047 pools ALL clients' set-aside buffers into one global setAsideBufferRecipient: in a multi-client deployment every non-recipient client's dip-absorption reserve is silently routed to the single recipient, while stale story-042 NatSpec still promises a per-client reserve
classifiedFindings.plausibility: n/a (not a High; no attacker at all — distributional routing among protocol-owned contracts)
classifiedFindings.fileLine: ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:353-372 (single aggregate safeTransfer to setAsideBufferRecipient — source-verified); ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:308-326; AYieldStrategy.sol:51-53 (stale per-client-reserve NatSpec — source-verified), :318-341 (setSetAsideBuffer still reads per-client), :352-357 (recipient setter); IYieldStrategy.sol:130-132 (stale)

classification.assetImpact: No value leaves the protocol. Tier-3 conservation PASS (totalSetAside <= underlyingReceived, dust to skim recipient); realized SURPLUS only is redirected, principal accounting untouched. The hazard is DISTRIBUTIONAL inside the protocol's own books: with story-047, the set-aside is never returned to the contributing client — it is summed across all clients and sent to the one global setAsideBufferRecipient. In a multi-client deployment, a non-recipient client whose underwater-exit machinery expects its own buffer back (the superseded story-042 semantics, still promised by the setAsideBufferSize NatSpec) finds its reserve silently subsidizing the recipient, and its underwater withdrawals can revert for lack of buffer.
attackPath: 1. (Owner config, future multi-client deployment) Owner authorizes two or more clients on one strategy and sets nonzero setAsideBufferSize for more than one of them — plausible because setSetAsideBuffer is per-client and its NatSpec still describes a per-client reserve.
2. Owner sets setAsideBufferRecipient to the address serving client A (e.g. stable-staker's buffer).

3. On every skimSurplus, _distributeBuffer sums ALL clients' set-asides and transfers the aggregate to the single recipient (ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol:368); client B's dip-absorption reserve never reaches client B.

4. Client B's underwater-exit path, sized against the documented story-042 reserve, reverts or under-delivers when the dip arrives. Funds are not lost — they sit at the recipient — but B's availability assumption is broken until manually rebalanced.
5. No external attacker exists anywhere in this path; every actor is the owner or a protocol-owned client.
classification.likelihood: low — requires a multi-client deployment (current intended deployment is one-client-per-strategy feeding stable-staker) AND multi-client nonzero buffer config AND a client integration relying on the stale per-client semantics. Each is plausible individually precisely because of the misleading setter shape and NatSpec, but the stack is conditional.
classification.assumptions: Clients are protocol-owned and owner-curated. story-047's intended deployment (single client funneling to stable-staker) is safe by construction; the hazard only materializes under future multi-client config.
classification.externalRequirements: None. Entirely internal configuration; no external party can trigger or profit.

classifiedFindings.lawBasis: Law-3 non-obvious owner footgun (FAITH-15-006 independently retained the same footgun at Low). Surprise test PASSES: the per-client setSetAsideBuffer setter and its NatSpec ('returned to the client... a reserve to absorb below-par dips') actively teach the owner the wrong model; a competent, non-malicious owner configuring a second buffered client would be surprised that client's reserve is routed away. NOT an unsafe story (Law-1/Law-2 check passed in FAITH-15-006): the implementation is FAITHFUL to story-047, redirect is explicit and loudly documented on the recipient side, and story-047 actually removes the old front-run-the-skim self-benefit incentive.
classifiedFindings.documentationCheck: NOT-BLESSED. knownIssuesCount=0. No designDecision mentions a buffer recipient or cross-client routing (story-047 postdates the registry extraction of 2026-01-23). The AUDITOR NOTE at AYieldStrategy.sol:325-335 blesses the adjacent deposit-weighting quirk, not cross-client recipient routing. No systemAssumption covers multi-client buffer configuration.

severityRationale.notHigh: No assets stolen/lost/compromised: surplus moves between protocol-owned addresses, conservation verified, no external attacker exists.
severityRationale.notMedium: The availability impact (a non-recipient client's underwater exits reverting) requires a stacked hypothetical: a multi-client deployment that does not exist at ad12cb1, plus a buffer misconfig against the intended topology, plus a client integration built on superseded story-042 semantics. C4 Medium with stated assumptions still requires the impacted surface to exist; here it is speculative future config. Honest floor is Low.
severityRationale.landsLow: Non-obvious owner config hazard with concrete safe-config guidance plus a doc-conflict that actively misleads (two NatSpec blocks in the same file contradict each other). Classic Law-3 footgun at Low, with the doc leg carried as F-04.

classifiedFindings.tier3Evidence: bufferConservation PASS under forge (256x250) and Medusa (200k tests): totalSetAside <= underlyingReceived, exact two-transfer split, dust to skim recipient. Distributional only; no value creation or leak.
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Safe config: set nonzero setAsideBufferSize ONLY for the client that is (or funnels to) the setAsideBufferRecipient; consider an on-chain guard rejecting nonzero buffers for clients other than the recipient's funnel, or making the recipient per-client. Fix stale NatSpec at AYieldStrategy.sol:51-53 and IYieldStrategy.sol:130-132 to state buffers are protocol-level yield routing to setAsideBufferRecipient, not client reserves (F-04, single combined doc-fix item with FAITH-15-003).
classifiedFindings.justification: Faithful-to-story distributional routing whose per-client setter shape and stale NatSpec set a non-obvious multi-client trap; value conserved inside the protocol, no attacker, hazard contingent on future config — Low operational footgun with safe-config guidance, doc leg routed to spec-conformance as F-04.
classifiedFindings.noOverstatement: Confirmed. Candidate Low confirmed at Low; the conditional availability angle was weighed for Medium and rejected as speculative future config.
